title: The Mystery of the Locked Hut
markdown:
The first snow tumbled down, hushing the woods. Tuppence, a snowshoe bunny with fur like frosted glass, twitched his nose. Mira, a sleek pine marten, uncoiled from a log. Sol, a rook black as ink, cawed from a pine.

“A fresh canvas,” Sol boomed, circling. “Games to be played.”

Tuppence hopped closer. “It’s so quiet.” A shiver. The hush felt larger than weather.

Mira’s sharp eyes found them. “Footprints.” Her tail flicked.

Stark against the snow marched a line of prints. Not theirs. Roundish, with circles and squares, heading deeper.

“Towards the old clearing,” Mira noted. The tumbled shed. It always held a maybe.

“Let’s go,” Sol chirped, already down. “Secret treasure?”

Tuppence hesitated. “What if it’s dangerous?” Caution was his old coat. The mystery tugged at the sleeve.

They followed through the hushed woods. Snow squeaked under Tuppence in a language only bunnies speak. Mira read the prints as if they were a letter: not a fox, not a deer, something that had worn boots and thought about stars. Sol flew ahead and back, impatient as punctuation. The line led to a sturdy hut among tall pines, a place the clearing had been keeping. A solid wooden door. A gleaming iron lock that looked too proud for a shed.

“Locked tight.” Sol pecked. Clang. Clang.

Mira circled. “No other door. Sealed.”

“What’s inside?” Tuppence’s ears drooped. “Why lock it so?”

Snow fell harder, a curtain threatening the clue. Wind whispered hurry.

They examined the lock. A tiny crescent-moon keyhole, too fine for Sol’s beak and too proud for a kick. Sol’s twig snapped in the attempt, a sound like a small disappointment. Mira sniffed iron, found old cold and a hint of lamp-oil, nothing of fox. Snow thickened, erasing the last prints even as they watched. Tuppence, usually first to retreat, felt a spark that was not fear: the puzzle wanted a careful paw, and he had two.

“Wait.” Mira pointed at the doorframe. “Faint scratches. Almost invisible.”

“Damage?” Sol cocked his head.

“Not random. Like instructions.”

Tuppence leaned in. “Left to right. Then down.”

“Left, right, down. A code?”

Sol squawked, wings up. “The rhyme. Left for the moon, right for the sun, down for the star, your puzzle is won.”

Tuppence’s eyes widened. “The keyhole is a moon.”

Mira smiled. “The grain around it looks like sunbeams. The scratch down points like a falling star.”

“How do we do it?” A shadow of worry returned. The snow was blizzard-thick. Last chance.

“The lock has grooves,” Mira said. “Push one way, then the other.”

“I see them.” Sol hopped onto the iron. “Left groove first, then right.”

Tuppence was not the strongest. His paws were steady. He set one on the left groove. Freezing metal bit fur. He pushed left. Nothing.

“The right,” Mira urged.

He shifted, pushed right. Still nothing. Disappointment flickered. Then: “Down for the star.”

Mira pointed to a faint star-shaped indentation. “There.”

He pressed down. The cold metal seemed to hold its breath. A soft click. A tiny movement.

“It moved,” Sol shouted. “We did it.”

Mira nudged the door. It creaked, releasing stale papery air, dust and dried ink. Inside, shadows clung to walls lined with strange brass instruments that gleamed faintly. A worn leather book lay open on a wooden desk, pages crinkling in the draft. Not gold. A forgotten observatory.

Tuppence pointed at the logbook. The last entry: First snow today. A perfect night for observing. Must remember to secure the hut. The stars await.

The footprints were a scientist’s own reminder, passion for the cosmos written in snow. The key had been knowledge, and a small courage.

They stepped out. The snow had erased the prints. It did not matter. Tuppence stood a little taller. Later, when a gust threatened a precious dried leaf Mira had found, he did not hesitate. He dashed, shielding it with his own small body, ears high, no longer twitching for worry, but for the next interesting thing the woods might write in white.
characters: Tuppence (a snowshoe bunny), Mira (a pine marten), Sol (a rook)
